**1. Staff accountability — the genuine thread.** Last year, D'Andrea — his ally, handing him Distinguisheds — named exactly one improvement area: "holding staff accountable and school building visitations." This year the board screams it: "accountability must be more than a slogan," "increased accountability for self and staff," staff "need approval for every routine decision." When your friend and your enemy independently name the same weakness 14 months apart, that's not politics. That's the thing that's actually true.

**2. Fiscal competence — the conceded strength.** D'Andrea praised his "understanding of CBA contracts, and overall business principles." DiNunno's demolition lists "fiscal responsibility" as strength number one. A hostile board doesn't hand your guy his best compliment unless it's undeniable. The money is fine; the man is the problem.

Everything else that flipped 180° — communication was his "extremely effective" superpower last year, now it's his worst category near Failing — that's where the politics live. Skills don't invert like that in a year; relationships do. The board isn't rating a changed Wallace. It's rating a broken relationship.

The caveat on all of it: neither document contains a single verifiable fact. No scores, no budgets, no incident counts. They're opinion instruments, so "factual accuracy" is doing heavy lifting. The closest either gets to fact is concession-against-interest — and on that test, exactly two things survive: he can't hold staff accountable, and he can handle money.
